refit.title: PLOS ONE · Ремонтаж каменных находок Лагар-Велью
refit.passage: Refit 31 reconstructs a quartzite cobble from core, seven flakes and one fragment. Refits can link excavation squares. Authors caution that links alone do not demonstrate simultaneous use of different areas.

remRu.title: Российская археология · Пример ремонтажа каменного орудия
remRu.passage: Article uses the term ремонтаж for physically reconstructing a fragmented lithic object.

chain.title: Internet Archaeology · Операционная последовательность в изучении каменных орудий
chain.passage: Explains chaîne opératoire as operational sequence from acquiring raw material through reduction, manufacture, use and discard. The framework reconstructs decisions in production and use.

kam.title: Институт археологии и этнографии СО РАН · Каменное украшение из эпипалеолита Камчатки
kam.passage: Russian abstract uses «операционная последовательность» to describe reconstruction of making a stone ornament with technological and experimental traceology plus 3D modeling.

bone.title: Оксфордский университет · Костяные ретушёры североафриканского среднего каменного века
bone.passage: Primary study reconstructs production, use and discard of 18 bone retouchers in dated layers and compares their form and function over time.

old.title: Historic England · Байесовский процесс и пригодность образцов
old.passage: Old-wood section explains the carbon in a ring dates to its growth. A sample from the middle of a long-lived oak may be centuries older than death and use. Short-life material can reduce this offset.

c14.title: Historic England · Радиоуглеродное датирование
c14.passage: Sections 1.2, 1.5, 1.6 describe exogenous carbon introduced by conservation and packaging, preparation for measurement, calibration from a known-age curve, and marine reservoir offsets that vary by place and time.

quality.title: Historic England · Байесовское хронологическое моделирование
quality.passage: The modeling guidance distinguishes the standardized likelihood of a radiocarbon result, Bayesian estimates, and agreement. Example dates can be simulated from a calendar age, calibration curve and measurement error. It also explains model down-weighting for outliers and hypothetical phase boundary estimates.

obs.title: PLOS ONE · Источники обсидиана в доколониальной Новой Зеландии
obs.passage: X-ray fluorescence compared trace element distributions in archaeological volcanic glass and reference sources. The paper examines multiple site types and discusses distribution and transport as inferences.

context.title: Служба национальных парков США · Археологический контекст
context.passage: Provenience and associations help relate an object to its stratigraphic location, other artifacts and ecofacts. Different site formation processes can change the original context.

quarry.title: Висконсинский университет в Ла-Кроссе · Анализ каменных находок
quarry.passage: Shows core, waste flakes, hammerstone, bifaces, points, end scraper, drill and utilized flake as distinct archaeological material. Sorting lithic objects helps interpret activity and technology.

type.title: Служба национальных парков США · Как археологи узнают возраст памятника
type.passage: Explains types of evidence and comparisons, depositional stratigraphy, dates of artifacts as limits on deposition and tree-ring dating.

trace.title: Институт археологии РАН · Трасология
trace.passage: Explains microscopy-based recording of wear on archaeological tools, including scratches, damage and polish.

note: CURRENT removes reciprocal notes across 073–075 and 096 and changes 072 and 096 to ask for their actual type of procedure. The six cards share one reviewer packet.
